desc: Read input, compress the values of $A$ to the range $[1, M]$ where $M \le N$, and store original queries.
Sort queries by $R_i$ to process them in increasing order of the prefix length.
Initialize a Fenwick tree (BIT) of size $M$ that supports point update (max) and prefix max query.

Iterate through the sorted queries. For each query with right endpoint $R$, add all elements $A_1, \dots, A_R$ that haven't been added yet: for each $A_j$, query the BIT for max value in range $[1, \text{compressed}(A_j)-1]$, add 1, and update the BIT at position $\text{compressed}(A_j)$ with this new length.

For each query $(R_i, X_i)$, after ensuring all elements up to $R_i$ are in the BIT, query the BIT for the maximum value in the range $[1, \text{compressed}(X_i)]$ (handling $X_i$ larger than max $A$ by clamping to max compressed value).
Store the answers and print them in the original order of queries.
